Below is a practical “cook‑book” style walk‑through for building your own desktop computer from scratch – whether you’re aiming for gaming, content creation, everyday use, or even a tiny home server. Feel free to skip parts that already fit your needs; I’ve kept it modular so you can pick what’s relevant. --- ## 1️⃣ Plan Your Build | What | Why It Matters | |------|----------------| | **Budget** | Determines component quality/price balance. | | **Primary Use** | Gaming → high‑end GPU, fast SSDs.
Office / light tasks → integrated graphics, modest specs.
Content creation → powerful multi‑core CPU, plenty of RAM. | | **Form Factor** | Full tower vs mid‑tower vs mini‑ITX affects space/cooling. | | **Future Upgrades** | Pick a motherboard with extra PCIe slots, M.2 bays, enough DDR slots. | ### Quick Decision Matrix | Scenario | Suggested Specs (approx.) | |----------|---------------------------| | Home Office | Ryzen 5 5600G / Intel i5‑12400F, 8GB RAM, 240GB NVMe, GTX 1650 Super | | Mid‑range Gamer | Ryzen 7 5800X / Intel i7‑12700K, 16–32GB RAM, RTX 3060 Ti, 500GB NVMe + 1TB HDD | | High‑End Content Creator | Threadripper PRO / Xeon W‑3175x, 64+ GB ECC RAM, dual RTX 3090, 2×NVMe 2TB, RAID 10 HDDs | | Tiny Server | AMD EPYC 7302P, 128GB DDR4 ECC, 2×SATA SSD, low‑power PSU | *(Prices fluctuate—use sites like PCPartPicker.com to compare current deals.)* --- ## 2️⃣ Gather Components | Category | Typical Choices | Notes | |---------|-----------------|-------| | **CPU** | AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, Intel Core i9‑13900KS | Check socket compatibility (AM5, LGA1700). | | **Motherboard** | X670E ATX, Z690 Mini‑ITX | Look at VRM cooling, expansion slots, Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth if desired. | | **RAM** | Corsair Vengeance RGB Pro 32GB DDR5‑6000 | Ensure speed matches motherboard support. | | **GPU** | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080, AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT | Verify length fits case clearance. | | **Storage** | Samsung 980 Pro 1TB NVMe, Seagate IronWolf NAS HDD 4TB | Keep SSD as primary drive for OS. | | **Power Supply** | Seasonic Focus GX‑850 Gold, EVGA SuperNOVA 750 G5 | Choose wattage ≥ 20% above estimated draw. | | **Case** | NZXT H710i, Fractal Design Meshify C | Good airflow, cable routing options. | | **Cooling** | Noctua NH-D15, Corsair Hydro Series H100i | Air vs liquid depends on noise tolerance. | | **Operating System** | Windows 11 Pro OEM key, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS ISO | Dual‑boot optional. | *Tip:* If you’re unsure, start with a pre‑built system and disassemble it to see how everything sits together before buying individual parts. --- ## 3️⃣ Assemble Step‑by‑Step > ⚠️ *Safety first*: Ground yourself (anti‑static wrist strap) and work on a non‑conductive surface. ### 3.1 Prep Workspace - Clean desk, gather screwdrivers (Phillips #0/#1), anti‑static mat, thermal paste (if not pre-applied). - Lay out all screws and small parts; keep them organized. ### 3.2 Install the CPU 1. Lift the CPU socket lever on the motherboard. 2. Align the gold triangle corner of the processor with the socket indicator. 3. Place gently, lower the lever back down. 4. Apply a pea‑size amount of thermal paste (or use a pre‑applied pad). ### 3.3 Mount the Cooler - For air coolers: attach mounting brackets to the rear panel, then secure onto the motherboard using the supplied screws. - For AIO water blocks: mount the block over the CPU, connect pump/fan cables later. ### 3.4 Insert RAM Modules - Unlock DIMM slot latches. - Snap sticks firmly until latch clicks back. ### 3.5 Secure the Motherboard Inside the Case - Position standoffs according to the motherboard layout. - Screw the board lightly; don’t overtighten yet. ### 3.6 Install the Power Supply - Slide PSU into its compartment, align fan direction outward. - Fasten with screws; route main connectors toward the motherboard. ### 3.7 Attach Storage Drives - Mount NVMe SSDs in dedicated M.2 slots; secure with screws. - Hook SATA data/data cables to the motherboard and SATA power cables from PSU for HDDs/SSDs. ### 3.8 Install Graphics Card - Remove appropriate PCIe riser bracket(s) from the case. - Slot GPU into topmost PCIe x16 slot; lock it in place. - Connect one or two 8-pin EPS cables from PSU to GPU. ### 3.9 Manage Cabling - Route cables neatly along designated pathways. - Tidy up with zip ties or Velcro straps. - Avoid blocking fans or vents. ### 3.10 Double‑Check Connections - Confirm all power connectors (ATX12V, 24‑pin, PCIe, SATA) are seated. - Make sure front panel headers match (USB, audio, reset button). ### 3.11 Close the Case - Replace side panels, tighten screws evenly. - Plug in monitor, keyboard, mouse, and power cord. --- ## 4️⃣ First Boot & Setup | Task | How | |------|-----| | **Enter BIOS/UEFI** | Press `Del` or `F2` during POST. | | **Set Date/Time** | Adjust under “System Information.” | | **Enable XMP Profile** | In Memory settings, enable profile matching your RAM spec. | | **Boot Order** | Set USB/DVD as first device if installing OS via external media. | | **Save & Exit** | Save changes (`Ctrl+S`) and reboot. | After successful POST, insert your OS installer (Windows DVD/USB or Linux live USB): 1. Follow on-screen prompts to format partitions. 2. Install drivers after OS boots (chipset, GPU, network). 3. Update firmware (BIOS, GPU microcode) through official utilities. --- ## 5️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Symptom | Likely Cause | Remedy | |--------|--------------|--------| | **PC doesn’t POST** | Loose power connector, wrong orientation, missing CMOS battery. | Recheck all plugs, reseat CPU cooler, replace CMOS battery. | | **Random Blue Screen** | Overclocked memory beyond stability limits. | Disable XMP or reduce frequency. | | **Fan Noise** | Dust accumulation or misaligned blades. | Clean filters, reorient fans. | | **Thermal Throttling** | Poor heatsink contact or inadequate airflow. | Reapply thermal paste, add more intake/outlet fans. | | **Display Issues** | Incorrect GPU seating or faulty HDMI port. | Reseat card, test another display output. | --- ## 6️⃣ Resources & Further Reading | Resource | Type | Link | |----------|------|------| | **PC Part Picker** | Parts comparison & price tracking | https://pcpartpicker.com | | **Tom’s Hardware Build Guides** | Video tutorials | https://www.tomshardware.com/category/build-guides | | **Reddit r/buildapc** | Community Q&A | https://reddit.com/r/buildapc | | **AnandTech Benchmarks** | Performance reviews | https://bench.anandtech.com | | **Linus Tech Tips** | Assembly walkthroughs | https://youtube.com/user/LinusTechTips | --- ### 🎉 Congratulations! 🎉 Your custom-built machine should now be ready to run games, edit video, crunch numbers, or serve files—all tailored exactly to your needs. Remember to keep your drivers updated, clean dust periodically, and enjoy the satisfaction of having built something entirely yours. Happy computing!
message.reasoning:
The user asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions or guidance. We can provide steps and considerations.

We might also ask clarifying questions about budget, usage (gaming, office), but we could give general guide. Provide components list, assembly steps, tips. Also mention safety precautions, cable management, BIOS setup, drivers installation.

Let's produce an answer with sections:

1. Planning & Budget
2. Component selection:
   - CPU
   - Motherboard
   - RAM
   - GPU
   - Storage
   - Power Supply
   - Case
   - Cooling
3. Building Steps:
   - Prepare workspace
   - Install motherboard into case
   - Mount CPU + cooler
   - Insert RAM
   - Attach power supply
   - Connect storage drives
   - Add GPU
   - Cable connections
   - Final checks
4. First boot & OS install
5. Troubleshooting common issues
6. Tips & resources

Also maybe link to guides like Tom's Hardware, YouTube videos etc.

No need to call tool because no recipe needed. So just respond directly.
